population.span: Eligible patients had chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction for at least 3 months, a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45% or less, and evidence of serum iron deficiency (had a serum ferritin level <100 ng/mL; or if transferrin saturation was <20%, had a serum ferritin level between 100 ng/mL and 299 ng/mL).

endpoint.span: Total (first and recurrent) hospitalizations for heart failure, No. of occurrences (rate/100 patient-years)

estimate.span: The second primary end point of total heart failure hospitalizations occurred 264 times in the ferric carboxymaltose group compared with 320 times in the placebo group (RR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60-1.06], P = .12).

ci.span: The second primary end point of total heart failure hospitalizations occurred 264 times in the ferric carboxymaltose group compared with 320 times in the placebo group (RR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60-1.06], P = .12).

analysis_set.span: The statistical analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle.

treatment_strategy.span: Administration of ferric carboxymaltose (n = 558) initially given at an intravenous dose of up to 2000 mg that was followed by 500 mg every 4 months (unless stopping criteria were met) vs a saline placebo (n = 547).

follow_up.span: The overall median follow-up was 16.6 months (IQR, 7.9-29.9 months). For parts A-C, the median follow-up was 17.3 months (IQR, 8.2-30.9 months) in the ferric carboxymaltose group vs 16.0 months (IQR, 8.7-28.7 months) in the placebo group.

served_mismatch: The served numerical estimate and confidence interval match total first and recurrent heart-failure hospitalizations in the intention-to-treat analysis. The source defines RR as rate ratio, consistent with the row's IRR label; served_outcome.served_estimand = HR is incorrect. This estimate is not a hazard ratio or a binary risk ratio.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Entry required chronic HFrEF with LVEF ≤45% and iron deficiency; the held registry specifies minimum age 18 years, and the reported analysis follows intention-to-treat.
